THE EVERYDAY ESSENTIALS

Small things that matter.

A few gentle starting points.
Make them your own, at your family’s pace.

☀01 / ROUTINES

A familiar rhythm

Give everyday moments a comforting pattern. A song while getting ready or a story at the end of the day can become something to look forward to.

Try today
Let your child choose the bedtime book.

♡02 / CONNECTION

Make space to listen

Put distractions aside for a little time together. Let your child tell you, show you, or draw what’s on their mind, without rushing to find an answer.

Try today
Ask, “What made you smile today?”

✳03 / INDEPENDENCE

Little helping hands

Invite children into simple everyday tasks that suit their abilities. Stay nearby, offer encouragement, and leave room for things to be imperfect.

Try today
Sort clean socks or tidy books together.

LESS PLANNING. MORE PLAY.

Turn “what now?”
into time together.

No special supplies. No perfect results.
Just pick an idea and follow their curiosity.

Adapt activities to your child’s abilities and stay nearby.

A SPARK OF IMAGINATION

YOU’RE NOT THE ONLY ONE WONDERING

A little reassurance.

Every child and every family is different.
There’s room to find what works for yours.

What if we only have a few minutes together?

Keep it simple: share a story, talk while putting things away, or notice something interesting on a walk. Choose a moment when you can give your child your attention.

Does every day need a full schedule?

Try a loose rhythm around familiar moments, with room for rest, changes, and child-led play. A routine can help you organize the day without filling every minute.

What if my child doesn’t want to join an activity?

Offer a choice, watch what interests them, or try again another time. Being together can be as simple as sitting nearby while they show you what they enjoy.

Where can I find more parenting guidance?

Explore UNICEF Parenting for further reading. For questions about your child’s health or development, speak with a qualified healthcare professional.
